title: The Vector of New Lagos
premise: Sable Lockridge, an insurance investigator who specializes in 'impossible accidents,' has quietly maintained an orbital beacon in New Lagos orbit for years — a beacon with no owner on record. When a cargo ship that officially never flew appears in the manifests carrying a passenger name that shouldn't exist, her investigation reveals the beacon is a dead-man's-switch courier system built by a peace faction inside the warring Meridian Combine. The message it carries can expose the war's true architects and force an armistice — but delivering it will also destroy Sable's legal identity and the life she's built. Hunted by Combine enforcers and betrayed by the man she loves, a duty-bound naval officer named Idris Kane, Sable must choose between the law that made her and the justice the beacon demands; in the end she broadcasts the message at terrible personal cost, toppling the war's profiteers but losing Kane to his own duty, and walks into New Lagos as someone new.
about_author: Dominic Voss is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal apartment where he still keeps a decommissioned lighthouse lamp as a desk ornament.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She performs her monthly maintenance run on an unregistered orbital beacon, noting its impossible paperwork trail. Establishes her meticulous, lonely competence and quiet curiosity about who built it. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cross-referencing claims files, she finds the freighter Halcyon Step listed as scrapped nine years ago — yet it docked last week. A single unfamiliar passenger name, 'Veyra Osei,' appears on its manifest. Beat: the hook tightens; professional thrill.

chapters.title: Impossible Accidents
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Flashback woven through present: how she earned her reputation proving three 'accidents' were sabotage, and why she trusts patterns over people. Introduces her handler, Okonkwo, who warns her off the Halcyon Step. Beat: defiance kindling.

chapters.title: The Passenger Named Veyra Osei
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She traces Veyra Osei to a records void — a person with no birth registration, no death certificate, yet active biometric pings in New Lagos' undercity. Beat: dread mixed with exhilaration of the hunt.

chapters.title: Idris
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Naval intelligence officer Idris Kane reviews the same anomaly from the Combine's side, ordered to find and silence whoever is asking questions. He recognizes Sable's investigative signature — they were lovers years ago. Beat: duty versus old love.

chapters.title: Downwell
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She descends into New Lagos' undercity following Osei's biometric ghost, navigating debt-bond districts and black-market clinics. First sign she's being followed. Beat: claustrophobic tension.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She finds Veyra Osei — alive, terrified, hiding in a chapel of the Long Silence sect. Osei claims to be a courier who smuggled herself off the Halcyon Step before it was 'disappeared.' Beat: revelation, fragile alliance.

chapters.title: What the Halcyon Carried
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. She explains: the ship carried proof that the war's opening strike was staged by the Combine's own Armaments Directorate, and that the beacon is a dead-man's-switch meant to broadcast it. Beat: the world tilts; moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Signal Integrity
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She verifies Osei's data chip against the beacon's handshake codes — they match. The beacon was built for exactly this message. Someone killed everyone who knew. Beat: cold certainty replacing doubt.

chapters.title: The Man from Claims
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Kane closes in on Sable's location, torn between orders and affection. He delays his report by six hours — a small treason. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Six Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Using Kane's delay, Sable and Osei reach a safehouse run by retired beacon engineer Mama Adeyemi, who helped build the switch. Beat: brief warmth, found family.

chapters.title: The Architect's Handshake
chapters.summary: Mama Adeyemi's POV. She reveals the beacon's creator: Director-General Cassius Renholt himself, before his corruption — he built the failsafe against his own institution. Beat: tragic irony; power devouring its maker.

chapters.title: Terms of Service
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Okonkwo resurfaces, offering Sable immunity if she surrenders the chip — the firm is compromised. She realizes her employer was laundering the war's insurance payouts. Beat: betrayal; the law revealed as complicit.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. His six-hour delay is discovered. His superior, Commander Vashti, gives him one chance: deliver Sable personally or be charged. Beat: the walls closing; love weaponized against him.

chapters.title: The Undercity Run
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable/Kane POV. Chase through flooded transit tunnels as Combine enforcers corner the safehouse. Kane arrives — ostensibly to arrest her. Beat: kinetic action, hearts pounding in both senses.

chapters.title: Point of No Return
chapters.summary: Sable and Kane face each other in the tunnels. She shows him the evidence; he must choose. He lets her go and falsifies his report — full defection now. Beat: love choosing duty to truth over duty to rank.

chapters.title: What Vashti Knows
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. Revealed as a war profiteer's ally, she escalates: declares Sable a terrorist, puts a kill order out. Beat: villainy unveiled; stakes become mortal.

chapters.title: The Chapel of the Long Silence
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. The sect offers sanctuary but their elder warns that broadcasting the message will trigger the Combine's contingency: scuttling New Lagos' orbital ring, killing thousands. Beat: the cost made flesh; hope bruised.

chapters.title: Collateral Mathematics
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She runs the numbers like an investigator: thousands die if she broadcasts; the war grinds on, tens of thousands more die over years if she doesn't. Beat: the book's moral crucible, laid bare.

chapters.title: Renholt's Ghost
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Kane infiltrates Directorate archives and finds Renholt's private logs — the old man foresaw his own corruption and left the beacon as penance. Beat: elegiac; understanding the enemy within.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Mama Adeyemi proposes a way to broadcast without triggering the scuttle protocol: physical access to the beacon's core, a manual override only two people alive can perform. One is Adeyemi. Beat: a door opens; cautious hope.

chapters.title: Recruitment
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV vignettes. Sable gathers allies: a disgraced ring engineer, an Osei-sympathetic chaplain, a smuggler pilot named Tunde. Beat: the heist crew assembles; camaraderie against despair.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Choice
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Cornered by the firm, he chooses to feed Sable the Directorate's security rotations — redemption purchased with his pension and safety. Beat: sacrifice; quiet heroism.

chapters.title: Upwell
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The crew ascends to orbit aboard Tunde's patched-together hauler, dodging a Combine picket line. Beat: breath-held tension; the plan in motion.

chapters.title: The Ring
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Kane, now openly hunted too, creates a diversion by surrendering himself to Vashti — buying the crew hours while feeding Vashti false beacon coordinates. Beat: love as strategy; terror under a calm mask.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Vashti interrogates Kane, offering him Sable's life in exchange for the real approach vector. He refuses. Beat: the theme crystallized — love against duty, inverted.

chapters.title: Airlock Ethics
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Boarding the beacon station, the crew discovers Vashti's enforcers already aboard — she anticipated them. Firefight in vacuum-adjacent corridors. Beat: the plan fraying; adrenaline and grief.

chapters.title: Mama Adeyemi Falls
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Adeyemi completes half the override sequence before taking a fatal shot, pressing the final key into Sable's hand: 'Finish my lighthouse.' Beat: devastating loss; inheritance of purpose.

chapters.title: The Override
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Alone at the core, Sable discovers the final step requires a living biometric signature registered to the beacon — Renholt's. It accepts hers instead: she was always its intended heir, hired years ago without knowing. Beat: destiny recontextualized; awe.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The broadcast begins its ten-minute cycle; Vashti triggers the scuttle protocol remotely. Tunde and the chaplain race to sever the ring's demolition uplink. Beat: split-screen desperation.

chapters.title: Vashti's Argument
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. Through an open channel she argues to Sable: the message ends nothing, only starts a civil war worse than this one. For one moment Sable wavers. Beat: the antagonist given her due; doubt's last stand.

chapters.title: The Vector
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable answers: justice delayed by fear is just corruption with better manners. She holds the transmit key down as the uplink severs behind her. The message goes out to every fleet, every colony. Beat: climax; irrevocable choice.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Silence
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. Fleets hold fire as the evidence propagates. Armistice talks convene within days. Osei, finally able to exist publicly, registers her name at last. Beat: exhale; tentative peace.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Trial of Idris Kane
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Kane faces court-martial. Sable's broadcast evidence exonerates his treason as justified whistleblowing — barely. He is stripped of rank and freed. Beat: justice outside the law vindicating itself inside it.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Vashti's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. Exposed by her own contingency orders, Vashti is arrested by officers she once commanded. She meets Sable once, in custody, and says nothing. Beat: power's corruption consuming itself.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable files one last insurance claim — for the Halcyon Step, its crew, and Mama Adeyemi — forcing the record to acknowledge the ship that never flew. Bureaucracy as memorial. Beat: grief given form; catharsis.

chapters.title: Two Lighthouses
chapters.summary: Kane and Sable, alternating POV. They meet at the undercity chapel. Both changed, both scarred, they admit the love neither duty nor war could erase — and agree to try again without promises. Beat: tender, earned reconciliation.

chapters.title: Decommissioned
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The beacon, its purpose fulfilled, is formally decommissioned. Sable requests custody of its transmitter core. She signs her resignation from the firm with her real name for the first time in the book. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Vector of New Lagos
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sable's POV. Months later, Sable runs a small investigative practice from the undercity, the beacon's core humming beside her desk as a private tip-line for the silenced. A new impossible case lands. Beat: resolution with forward motion; the light kept lit.

chapters.title: Author's Note: On Beacons
chapters.summary: Meta epilogue in Voss's voice. Reflections on the real-world maritime disasters and insurance frauds that inspired the novel, and why stories about people who keep lights burning matter. Beat: warmth; the author stepping out of the dark.
